name: Deliver a daily digest with Google Drive and Outlook for your team

nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 17:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Gather from Google Drive
nodes.notes: Searches Google Drive for matching files/folders — the discovery step before download or processing. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.

nodes.name: Gather from Outlook
nodes.notes: Polls the Outlook inbox for unread messages — the source step for an email-driven pipeline. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.

nodes.name: Gather API Numbers
nodes.notes: GET https://api.example.com/v1/events — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Blend Sources
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Roll Up KPIs
nodes.notes: Group-by + aggregate (like a pivot table) — turns raw rows into KPI numbers.

nodes.name: Compose HTML Report
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build an HTML digest table from the aggregated rows Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Send Report via Outlook
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Microsoft Outlook — recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Pulls every page from the Notion database — fine for small datasets; add a filter if the database grows large. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Copy to Google Drive
nodes.notes: Uploads the generated file to Google Drive as a timestamped archive copy. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.

nodes.name: Enrich with Reference Data
nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per event (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 25 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Sort Events Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty severity
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Event Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

# Deliver a daily digest: Outlook

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers escalations work end to end across Outlook, Notion, Google Drive and Google Sheets.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Gather from Google Drive
3. Gather from Outlook
4. Gather API Numbers
5. Blend Sources
6. Roll Up KPIs
7. Compose HTML Report
8. Send Report via Outlook
9. Stamp Completion Time
10. Persist Run Metadata
11. Load Previous Snapshot
12. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
13. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
14. Archive Copy to Google Drive
15. Enrich with Reference Data
16. Fold In Enrichment Fields
17. Fingerprint for Idempotency
18. Drop Already-Processed Items
19. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
20. Record Sub-workflow Result
21. Cap Batch Volume
22. Sort Events Newest First
23. Tag Pipeline Metadata
24. Save Execution Metadata
25. Guard Non-Empty severity
26. Align Field Names
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
29. Send Summary to Outlook

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing escalations work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Gather from Google Drive → Gather from Outlook → Gather API Numbers → Blend Sources → Roll Up KPIs → Compose HTML Report → Send Report via Outlook → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Copy to Google Drive → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Cap Batch Volume → Sort Events Newest First → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Save Execution Metadata → Guard Non-Empty severity → Align Field Names → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Outlook → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Outlook and Notion aligned by hand for escalations
- Escalations work where "Gather from Google Drive" is still a manual step before Outlook
- Escalations work that only reaches Outlook on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Outlook and Notion in step for escalations, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Outlook or Notion are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this escalations build
- A failed Outlook or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this escalations build
- Branches rejoin before Outlook, so a escalations run reports once rather than 32 times
- Every escalations run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Outlook

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

KPIs are rolled up with Summarize (exact group-by + aggregate) before any AI touches the data — asking an LLM to 'figure out the numbers' from raw records is slower, costlier, and less reliable than doing exact arithmetic in n8n and only asking the model to narrate numbers that are already correct.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a second data source and watch it blend into the same report via Merge.
2. Toggle the AI executive-summary step on and off and compare the report's usefulness.
3. Change the KPI grouping field and see how the pivot reshapes.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your escalations process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole escalations payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
